questions.question: What does this sign mean?
questions.correctAnswerText: A stop sign is ahead.
questions.explanation: Yellow warning signs have black lettering or symbols. They tell drivers about road conditions ahead. This sign warns you that a stop sign is coming.

questions.question: In a turn, rolling on the throttle helps you:

options.text: Keep or increase your speed and stabilize the motorcycle.

questions.correctAnswerText: Keep or increase your speed and stabilize the motorcycle.
questions.explanation: When turning, use the throttle to keep your speed steady or slightly increase it. This helps keep the motorcycle stable.

questions.question: When passing another vehicle, you:

options.text: May go 10 mph over the speed limit.
Must not exceed the speed limit.
Must ride faster than the speed limit.

questions.correctAnswerText: Must not exceed the speed limit.
questions.explanation: You must complete passes within the speed limit. Only pass where it is safe and legal.

questions.question: A motorized bike with less than 45 cubic centimeters displacement:

options.text: Cannot be operated on a public roadway.
Must be operated on the shoulder.

questions.correctAnswerText: Cannot be operated on a public roadway.
questions.explanation: In Nebraska, motorized bikes and motor scooters with engines smaller than 45 cubic centimeters, or with wheel and tire diameter less than 14 inches, cannot be operated on public roads.

questions.question: If you accidentally lock your rear brake on a surface with good traction, you should:

options.text: Keep the rear brake locked until you stop.
Release the rear brake and use only the front brake.

questions.correctAnswerText: Keep the rear brake locked until you stop.
questions.explanation: If the rear wheel locks on a surface with good traction, leave it locked until you stop completely. You can still control the motorcycle as long as it stays upright and goes straight.

questions.question: If your rear wheel locks while stopping on a surface with good traction, you should:

options.text: Keep the wheel locked until you have stopped completely.
Release the rear brake and use only the front brake.
Release the rear brake and quickly apply it again.

questions.correctAnswerText: Keep the wheel locked until you have stopped completely.
questions.explanation: When the rear wheel locks on good traction while stopping, keep it locked until you stop. You can control the motorcycle if it stays upright and travels straight.

questions.question: To control a motorcycle well, you should:

options.text: Use your arms to hold yourself up.
Keep your knees against the gas tank.
Sit with your arms straight when holding the handlebars.

questions.correctAnswerText: Keep your knees against the gas tank.
questions.explanation: Sit so you can use your arms to steer, not to hold yourself up. Your elbows should bend slightly at the handlebars. Keep your knees against the gas tank to help with balance.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: Vehicles will be entering the roadway.
Come to a complete stop and proceed when it is safe.

questions.correctAnswerText: Come to a complete stop and proceed when it is safe.
questions.explanation: Red octagonal signs are always stop signs. You must stop completely, check for traffic and pedestrians, and proceed only when it is safe.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?
questions.correctAnswerText: Merge
questions.explanation: Yellow warning signs have black lettering or symbols. They tell drivers about road conditions ahead. This sign warns of merging traffic.

questions.question: When riding in a group, the best formation to keep riders together with safe spacing is:
questions.correctAnswerText: A staggered formation.
questions.explanation: A staggered formation is best for group riding. It keeps riders close together while giving each rider enough space to stay safe.

questions.question: When you need to react to a hazard on the road, you should NOT:

options.text: Avoid telling other drivers about your presence.
Use your horn and/or lights or signals to alert other drivers.

questions.correctAnswerText: Avoid telling other drivers about your presence.
questions.explanation: To stay safe and reduce danger from hazards, let other drivers know you are there. Use your horn, lights, and signals. Slow down or speed up as needed. Change your lane position or direction to avoid the hazard.

questions.question: When looking through a turn, you should:

options.text: Turn only your head, not your shoulders.
Turn your head and shoulders to see better.
Turn your shoulders, but not your head.

questions.correctAnswerText: Turn only your head, not your shoulders.
questions.explanation: Look through the turn toward where you want to go. Turn only your head, not your shoulders. Keep your eyes level with the horizon.

questions.question: It is most important to flash your brake light when:

options.text: Another vehicle is following you too closely.

questions.correctAnswerText: You are slowing down suddenly.
questions.explanation: A motorcycle's brake light is not as bright as a car's brake light. Flash your brake light when you slow down or stop so other drivers will notice. This is especially important when you slow down faster than expected.

questions.question: When riding at night, keep a minimum following distance of:
questions.correctAnswerText: Three seconds.
questions.explanation: It is hard to judge distance in the dark. Stay at least three seconds behind the vehicle in front of you when riding at night.

questions.question: When entering a curve, position your motorcycle:

options.text: On the outside edge of the curve.
On the inside edge of the curve.
Where you can safely handle road and traffic conditions.

questions.correctAnswerText: Where you can safely handle road and traffic conditions.
questions.explanation: Each curve is different. Choose a lane position that works for current conditions and adjust as you need to.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?
questions.correctAnswerText: Right lane ends
questions.explanation: Warning signs are yellow with black letters or symbols. They tell drivers about road conditions ahead. This sign warns that the right lane is ending.

questions.question: Passengers should:

options.text: Look over their shoulder when taking a turn or curve.
Sit as far back as possible.

questions.correctAnswerText: Look over their shoulder when taking a turn or curve.
questions.explanation: Before your passenger gets on, ask them to look over your shoulder in the direction of turns or curves. This helps you and your motorcycle lean the right way.

questions.question: Small vehicles appear to be ________ and slower than they really are.
questions.correctAnswerText: Farther away
questions.explanation: It is hard to judge how fast a small vehicle is going and how far away it is. Do not assume that drivers of large vehicles can correctly judge your speed and location.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?
questions.correctAnswerText: No U-turn
questions.explanation: Regulatory signs are white with red and black markings. They tell drivers what traffic laws apply in that area. This sign means U-turns are not allowed.

questions.question: What does an integrated braking system do?

options.text: It connects the front and rear brakes when you use the rear brake.
It brakes automatically by learning your riding style.
It connects to the gears and applies the brake when you downshift.

questions.correctAnswerText: It connects the front and rear brakes when you use the rear brake.
questions.explanation: Some motorcycles have integrated braking systems. When you press the rear brake pedal, it uses both the front and rear brakes together. Check your owner's manual to learn about your specific motorcycle's brakes.

questions.question: Motorcycle riders must wear eye protection. Is this required?
questions.correctAnswerText: Yes, it is required.
questions.explanation: In Georgia, motorcycle riders must wear proper eye protection.

questions.question: When another vehicle is passing you from behind, which part of the lane should you ride in?
questions.correctAnswerText: Center
questions.explanation: The center of the lane is the safest position when being passed. Riding too far to the right risks a collision with the passing vehicle. Riding too far to the left may cause the other driver to swerve back into your lane too soon.

questions.question: What percentage of motorcycle crashes with cars are caused by drivers failing to give the right-of-way to the motorcycle?
questions.correctAnswerText: More than half
questions.explanation: More than half of crashes between motorcycles and cars happen because drivers do not give the right-of-way to motorcycles. Always assume that drivers may not yield, even if they are required to by law.

questions.question: If your front wheel locks up while braking, what should you do?

options.text: Release the front brake right away, then apply it again.
Release the front brake right away and only use the rear brake.
Keep the front wheel locked until you stop completely.

questions.correctAnswerText: Release the front brake right away, then apply it again.
questions.explanation: If the front wheel locks during braking, release the brake immediately and then apply it again.

questions.question: The oily strip in the center of a lane—is it safe to ride on?

options.text: Only if another vehicle is sharing the lane with you.
Yes, it is usually safe to ride on, except when it is raining.

questions.correctAnswerText: Yes, it is usually safe to ride on, except when it is raining.
questions.explanation: The oily strip usually gives enough grip for safe riding, except in rain. The strip is usually about two feet wide, so you can ride on either side of it while still staying in the center of the lane.
